Subject: [URGENT] Significant latency + 500s from us-west-2 - impact to dashboards

Ben,

We started seeing a large spike in tail latency and ~20% 500 responses for our analytics ingestion coming from US-WEST-2 beginning ~08:05 PST. Our alerts are firing and several dashboards are showing incomplete ingestion. We've attached a small snapshot of the error window (borealis_error_snapshot_0815.log).

This is customer-impacting; can you confirm whether this is an infrastructure routing issue on your side or something we need to remediate in our SDK? We're on a critical reporting run and need a mitigation within 30 minutes.

Please escalate immediately — our ops team (cc'd) is standing by.

Thanks,
Ellen

Borealis Analytics

Ben Carter

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@borealis.ai>, Tom Li <tom.li@borealis.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:23:37 -0800
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Significant latency + 500s from us-west-2 - impact to dashboards

Seen. Quick findings from initial telemetry:
- US-WEST-2 AZ3 shows sustained KV-cache write amplification starting ~08:02; token retrieval latencies spiked (p95 -> 1.2s).
- We’re observing an increase in transient 502/503 from the shard frontends; backend GPUs are healthy.
- Network metrics show intermittent packet retransmits concentrated to AZ3.

Recommended mitigation (low risk):
1) Start a controlled reroute: shift 20% of Borealis traffic to US-EAST-1 (canary) and monitor for 10 minutes.
2) If successful, increase to 60% and then fully failover for affected shard group.
3) Enable aggressive prefix-KV caching on the rerouted instances to reduce cold-cache penalty.

Attachment: kvcache-metrics-0818.png (small snapshot).

Risks: cold-cache on the target region will cause short-term latency for the first 1–2 minutes for some request patterns. We'll mitigate with warmed-up cache and prefetch hints where possible.

I can implement the routing change now if customer authorizes.

—Markus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
